summary: Computed a_p for the conductor-11 (11a) and conductor-37 (37a) elliptic newforms (a_p = -sum_x (f(x)/p), checked against known a_2,a_3,a_5,a_7,a_13) and correlated a_p/sqrt(p) with the BM residual (R-M_BM)/sqrt(M_BM) over the 8977 primes p≡1 (mod 4), p≤2·10^5: r = +0.0007 (11a) and -0.0127 (37a), |r| ≈ 1.2 standard errors. No Hecke-type correlation.
not_done: Only two newforms, no weight-12 Delta (a_p not computed), no twisted/residue-class-restricted correlation, no trace-formula identity attempted.
next: Repeat with Delta and conductors 15–100 up to 10^6 if a Hecke link is pursued.

summary: Analytic step: the defining relation 4uBC-u-B=p is cubic in (u,B,C), so R(p) is not a quadratic-lattice theta coefficient; per C the divisor form gives sum_{d|4Cp+1, d≡-1 (4C)} = (1/phi(4C)) sum_chi chibar(-1) sum_{d|N} chi(d) with N=4Cp+1, i.e. Eisenstein-type coefficients evaluated at 4Cp+1 rather than at p. Also d ≡ -1 (mod 4) for every certificate, so the chi_{-4}-signed count is trivially -R. Identity (4uC-1)(4BC-1)=4Cp+1 checked symbolically and in code (scripts assert d*e=4Cp+1).
not_done: No Siegel–Weil/weight computation; no test of a mock-theta or theta decomposition numerically.
next: Only if a quadratic space is written down for a fixed C (none found).

summary: Analytic: with a=4C the series sum_{u,B} q^{4CuB-u-B} = sum_u q^{(4C-1)u-1}/(1-q^{4Cu-1}) has coefficient of q^n equal to #{(u,B): 4CuB-u-B=n}; the substitution 4Cn+1=(4Cu-1)(4CB-1) turns it into the shifted divisor count #{d | 4Cn+1 : d≡-1 mod 4C}. The nonprincipal-character parts are Eisenstein-type, but the principal part sum_{N≡1(4C)} d(N) q^{(N-1)/4C} (a Lambert series in d(n)) is, by Assessment, not modular, so no exact Appell–Lerch closed formula is expected.
not_done: Did not check mock modularity numerically; claim about the principal part is Assessment.
next: None unless a modular completion is sought.

summary: Over the 4783 primes p≡1 (mod 4), p≤10^5, the continued-fraction period of sqrt(p) (= regulator-type quantity; always odd since N(eps)=-1) correlates with the BM ratio R/M_BM: corr(log period, R/M) = -0.12, and -0.069 after regressing out log p (≈4.7 naive standard errors). The sign and size are those expected if the effect is the L(1,chi_p) / regulator effect that BM_LVALUE.md documents (hard ⇔ large L(1,chi)); not separated here.
not_done: Class numbers h_p and L(1,chi_p) not computed, so the regulator-vs-L-value separation is untested; no smallest-certificate word analysis (ES₅ CF-length test) done.
next: Compute h_p·R_p = sqrt(p) L(1,chi_p)/2 and regress R/M on log L(1,chi_p) and log period jointly.

summary: Tropical points in [−3,3]³ of 4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx) with v_p(n)=1 (condition: min{a+b+c, 1+a+b, 1+b+c, 1+a+c} attained twice): 96 points; up to permutation the multisets are {0,0,1}, {0,1,1}, {0,2,2}, {1,1,1}, {1,2,2}, {2,2,2}. Realised valuation multisets of all positive solutions of 4/p for p≡1 (mod 4), p<120: only {0,0,1} (79 solutions, Type I) and {0,1,1} (47, Type II). The tropical variety is strictly larger: {1,1,1} is excluded by 1/x'+1/y'+1/z'=4 (no positive solution), and the {·,2,2} patterns (p² | two denominators) were not realised for p<120; only the {1,1,1} exclusion is proved here.
not_done: Tropical cones beyond the box [−3,3]³ not enumerated.

summary: Substitute measurement (disclosed): the e-slice ratio set {ab^{-1} mod e : ab|N} was not computed; instead D_C(p)={d mod 4C : d | 4Cp+1}. For the 105 hard primes (R/M<0.25, p≤10^6) and C≤30 (3150 slices): mean |D|/phi(4C)=0.28, the whole unit group is hit in only 42 slices, and -1 ∈ D in 91 slices (2.9%, i.e. the ES slice-success rate). For the 9 (★)-failures D never contains -1. The divisor residue sets are far from the whole group, so sum-product covering is not the operative regime.
not_done: e-slice ratio set not computed; no sum-product or Bourgain–Glibichuk–Konyagin bound applied; C≤30 only.
next: Recompute with the ratio set {ab^{-1}} and e up to 200 for hard primes.

summary: Restatement check: the subproduct set of the prime factors of N=4Cp+1 in (Z/4C)^× equals the divisor-residue set D_C(p) measured in Z1690. Whole-group events are rare (42 of 3150 hard slices, C≤30) and -1 is hit in 2.9%; with ω(N)≈log log N elements, Olson/EGZ-type zero-sum theorems (which need many elements) do not apply. Assessment.
not_done: No literature check of Olson-type bounds for multiplicative subsets of size ω(N).

summary: Analytic: at q=p the defining equation of U_p reduces to 4xyz ≡ 0 (mod p), so the F_p-shadow is degenerate and local solvability is trivial; no natural finite-field statement implying ES(p) with a size gap was identified.
not_done: No explicit F_p-curve or set construction tested.
next: None unless a concrete F_p statement is proposed.

summary: Analytic: the condition (4uC-1) | p+u is not a polynomial nonvanishing condition over F_ℓ in (u,C) (it is a divisibility of integers), so the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz has no polynomial to apply; no construction of a grid polynomial was found.
not_done: No symbolic coefficient computation (the object does not exist as stated).

summary: Exact count: for u·B≠0 the variety V_p: 4uBC-u-B=p over F_q has C uniquely determined, and the lines u=0 (B=-p) and B=0 (u=-p) contribute q points each; hence #V_p(F_q) = (q-1)^2+2q = q^2+1 for every p≢0 (mod q). The point count is independent of p, so the F_q-counts carry no p-dependence; all information is arithmetic (integrality), not geometric.
not_done: No brute-force F_q check was run (count is by hand).

summary: Same decomposition in K_0(Var): [V_n] = [G_m^2] + 2[A^1] = L^2 + 1 for every n≠0, independent of n; the variety is rational (C solved as (n+u+B)/(4uB)). Motivic classes do not see the integrality condition that carries ES.

Analytic: Descartes' relation for curvatures is quadratic (k4 = k1+k2+k3 ± 2 sqrt(k1k2+k2k3+k3k1)), whereas 1/x+1/y+1/z=4/p is linear in reciprocals; no literal embedding of ES into a circle configuration was found (Assessment).
Analytic only: Stern–Brocot/CF of 4/p has length of order log p and no ES criterion was identified in the tree positions; the run-length pattern was not computed.
not_done: SB paths and run-length statistics not computed.
next: Compute run-lengths of SB paths of 4/p for hard primes against R/M.

summary: Analytic: 1/x and 1/y are Farey neighbours iff |x-y|=1, so Farey edges among the terms of an Egyptian triple occur only for consecutive denominators; the Farey-path reading of ES is therefore degenerate.

Analytic check of the first step: the factorisations of a C-slice N_C=4Cp+1 = de with d≡e≡−1 (mod 4C) are the data of a binary quadratic object whose discriminant depends on C through N_C; there is no single discriminant D(p) attached to p alone among the slices. Assessment: a geodesic/equidistribution route needs a fixed D(p), so this route is not yet defined.
next: Propose a D(p) that is independent of C (none identified).

summary: Thue-type box test: for p≡1 (mod 4) the fraction of primes with NO certificate (4uB | p+u+B) having uB ≤ sqrt(p) is 10.0% (p<10^3), 6.2% (10^3–10^4), 3.2% (10^4–10^5), 1.2% (10^5–10^6). The Thue-size box alone is not a covering, and the failure fraction decays but is not zero at the scales checked.
not_done: No fixed modulus M(p) or residue a(p) searched; box test only.
next: Test a modulus-based Thue variant only if the box test's failures are structured.

summary: Splitting of x³−x−1 mod p (3 roots ⇔ split completely in the S_3 splitting field; roots counted by deg gcd(x^p−x, f), verified against brute force) over p≡1 (mod 4), p≤10^6: P(split) = 0.166 overall (Chebotarev 1/6) and 0.181 among the 105 hard primes (n small, not significant). Raw means R/M: 1.122 (split) vs 1.196 (one root), but this difference is entirely the quadratic character (−23/p): within (−23/p)=+1 the 3-root class has mean R/M 1.122 and the 0-root class 1.128. The non-abelian splitting carries no signal beyond ℚ(√−23).
not_done: Other non-abelian fields (e.g. x³−2) not tested.
next: Test a second cubic field with a different quadratic subfield if a non-abelian signal is wanted.

summary: Model check: the Weierstrass model E_N: Y²=X(X²+(N²−6N−3)X+16N) and the plane cubic C_N: (x+y+z)(xy+yz+zx)=N xyz have equal point counts over F_q for all 24 pairs (N,q), q∈{5,7,11,13}. Premise check: 'E_n attached to 4/n' is ill-defined: N=4(x+y+z)/n depends on the solution, and distinct solutions give distinct curves (p=37: 9 solutions → 9 distinct N). So there is no single curve per n, and the requested root-number/rank correlation has no well-defined input as stated.
not_done: No rank or root-number computation (the object was ill-defined at the first step, so none was run).
next: Restate the test per ES point (curve E_N for N=4(x+y+z)/n) and compute root numbers there.

summary: Analytic: no family E_p with w(E_p)=-1 for all relevant p and a map from points to certificates was proposed; parity forcing has no concrete input here (Assessment).
next: None unless a family is proposed.

summary: Analytic: no map from CM/Heegner points on X_0(N) to integer certificates was identified; the 'norm of a coordinate' question was not checked.
Analytic: abc gives Diophantine non-existence and radical-size bounds, not existence; the requested implication (abc ⇒ failure forces radical patterns) was not established and no data test was run.

Sanity item: B1 (Dickson/Schinzel H) gives infinitely many evaders of any fixed menu, so any proposed proof must use an unbounded menu. The observed (★)-failure list (9 primes ≡1 mod 4 up to 10^6, reproduced by scripts/z38 and matching BM_CORRECTED_COUNT) is consistent with this calibration; no new information.

Analytic: R(p) is an integral-point count, not a Frobenius trace; T(p)=sum (−uB/p)/phi(4uB) is a character sum but has no Deligne-type bound from a known motive. No Tate-module identification was made.

Janson-type lower-tail bound in a random-residue model for the box {4uB ≤ X} (events p ≡ -(u+B) mod 4uB): mu grows as ≈0.145 (log X)^2 (mu=13.55 at X=16000) while Delta/mu grows ≈0.5 log X (Delta/mu=5.0 at X=16000) because all moduli share the factor 4 and dependence is dense. Janson's bound exp(-mu^2/(2 Dbar)) = exp(-mu/(2(1+Delta/mu))) therefore decays only like X^{-c} (c≈0.14) rather than exp(-mu): the standard inequality is polynomial, not poly-logarithmic-exponential, in the box size. Model-level result; not a bound on the actual R(p).
not_done: Only the random-residue model was studied; no proof that the actual R(p) satisfies the model's dependency structure; no Suen or higher-order inequality tested.
next: Test whether a Janson-type bound improves after conditioning on the factor-4 structure (u,B parity classes).

summary: Heilbronn-type check: the mean Euclid/CF length of a/p over a∈[1,p) has slope 0.8440 in ln p on primes p∈[10³,10⁴] (Heilbronn constant 12 ln2/π² = 0.8428). The fraction of a with CF length ≤3 is a size-decreasing function of p (corr with ln p = −0.66) and its correlation with R/M (+0.19, p≤10^4) is confounded by size; no partial correlation done.
not_done: Partial correlation of the length-≤3 fraction with R/M after controlling ln p; Baladi–Vallée counts for ES₅ words not defined in the repo.
next: Compute the partial correlation and identify the ES₅ word count it should match.

summary: Analytic: the ES equation 4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx) is linear in each variable separately (not only bilinear); after y=x+s it becomes quadratic in x, so a Vieta move may exist, but no descent relation preserving positivity was identified.
next: Search for a Vieta involution with positive partner.

summary: Random-multiplicative model: approximating T(p) by sum_{m even ≤ p/4} (m/p)W(m), W(m)=2^ω(m)/(4φ(m)) (checked to ~10^-3 against exact T(p) at three primes near 10^5), and replacing (m/p) by a random completely multiplicative sign f: model spread matches the real spread on p∈(9·10^5,10^6]: sd 1.83 (300 draws) vs 1.81 real; quantiles 5/50/95%: model (−1.47, −0.04, 4.40), real (−1.58, −0.02, 4.66). The Rademacher model reproduces the distribution of T; no extra cancellation beyond it is visible.
not_done: Only the first-order model with the W approximation; no test of a Harper-type better-than-√ cancellation claim beyond the spread.
next: Compare higher moments and the joint law with R/M.

summary: Analytic: an incompressibility argument would need a counterexample to be of low description complexity; no such implication is available from the data (hardest-100 list is not low-complexity in an obvious sense). Assessment.

Analytic: Furstenberg-type ×2×3 rigidity gives orbit density in (Z/q)^× for the semigroup generated by 2,3, but the certificate needs -1 in the set of divisor classes of 4Cp+1, which is not an orbit of a fixed semigroup; no test done.

Greedy (Fibonacci–Sylvester) expansion of 4/p over p≡1 (mod 4), p≤10^5: length exactly 3 for 2399 primes and 4 for 2384 primes, i.e. a 3-term greedy ES certificate exists for about half of these primes (this is the trivial part of the picture; it is consistent with R(p)≥1). Partial correlation of greedy length with R/M given log p: +0.10 (not analysed further). Engel expansions (O150) are a different object and the greedy length is not a density heuristic for R.
next: Check whether the greedy success set is contained in the (★)-positive set (should be by construction).

summary: Analytic: a second-moment (Paley–Zygmund) positive-proportion statement over short intervals needs E[R^2]/E[R]^2 bounded on the interval, which requires variance information not computed here; EXCEPTIONAL_SHORT.md covers the exceptional-set side only.
next: Compute E[R^2]/E[R]^2 over intervals of length H = (log X)^A.

summary: Analytic: no lattice Λ_p in ℝ^3 with a small-cone-to-certificate correspondence was constructed; the SL_2 reading is in bsA_hecke_cusp_excursions.md and is not extended.

Least-squares fit of M0(p)=sum 1/phi(4uB) over all primes p∈[10^3,10^6] with M0 = a L^2 + b L + c, L=log p: a = 0.15203 (vs 3/(2π²)=0.15198, agreement 3·10^-4); fitted b ≈ -0.022 and c ≈ -0.19 are numerical, not derived by Mellin transform.
not_done: No Mellin/zeta-regularisation derivation of b and c.
next: Derive b and c via the Dirichlet series of sum 1/phi(4uB) and compare.

summary: Greedy Egyptian depth of every a/p (p≡1 mod 4, p≤2000, 147 primes): depth distribution 1:147, 2:1138, 3:10229, 4:29050, 5:42165, 6:32652, 7:14762,…; the average fraction of a with greedy depth ≤3 is 0.144. For a=4 the depth is 3 for 79 of 147 primes. The 'functional graph mod p' of the greedy map is not well defined (the denominator grows at each step, so the remainder leaves the set {a/p}); the depth distribution is the object that exists, and hard primes (only 2 in range) show no difference.
not_done: No hard-prime sample large enough to test depth against hardness.
next: Extend the depth census to hard primes up to 10^5.

summary: Data-based evader thresholds among the 395 primes p≡1 (mod 840), p≤10^6: the smallest prime with no certificate of modulus 4uB ≤ Q is 2521 for Q≤200, 3361 for Q=500, 12601 for Q≥1000. The fraction of these primes with no certificate of modulus ≤Q is 1.00 (Q≤50), 0.88 (Q=100), 0.69 (Q=200), 0.50 (Q=500), 0.35 (Q=1000), 0.13 (Q=5000): evaders are common at every size checked, so no menu of size Q up to 5000 is complete for this class at p≤10^6.
not_done: No CRT-constructed evader (the data-based threshold is the observed minimum, not the CRT minimum).
next: Run the CRT construction for Q up to 200 and compare with these thresholds.

summary: Analytic: the pair enumeration (u,B) for R(p) decides ES(p) with O(p log p) divisibility tests (no factoring), so the complexity of certificate search is polynomial in p, not polylogarithmic in p; the witnessing-theorem route therefore needs a polylog search that is not available.
not_done: No proof-complexity lower bound or Buss witnessing analysis.

summary: Premise check: divisor-form certificates need factoring only if one insists on the divisor form; the pair form (u,B) is searched by divisibility tests alone (as in scripts/z52d_p2_TO5_certs.c), so the 'factoring hardness' premise is false for the pair form. No conclusion about provability.
Analytic: no map from a set of size >N to size N whose collisions are certificates was identified; PPP framing gives no test.

Search programs over the pair set P(p) (p≡1 mod 4, p≤5000, 327 primes with a certificate; 2 without): 'scan pairs in a fixed order and stop at the first certificate'. Mean number of pairs examined: 31.2 for order by u+B, 35.5 for uB, 70.5 for B-then-u, 70.5 for u-then-B, 36.3 for max(u,B); medians are 1 for all orders, maxima 1280–2854. The order by u+B is the cheapest of those tested.
not_done: Only five orders tested; no learned or LLM-guided synthesis run.
next: Test orders from the slice-success tables (Z1856) in a larger search.

summary: ω(4Cp+1) over the 3420 slices (C≤30) of the hard primes and the (★)-failures: ω ∈ {1,…,6} with 443, 1250, 1194, 453, 77, 3 slices. Exhaustive subset enumeration then costs at most 2^6 = 64 subset products per slice, so exact enumeration is cheaper than any lattice reduction here; the size constraint d < √N is automatic in enumeration.
not_done: No LLL run (not needed for exact enumeration at these ω).

summary: Premise and step: for p=409 (a (★)-failure) the trial set P(409) has 272 pairs (68 distinct moduli 4uB) with sum 1/phi(4uB)=5.1506 (matches z38_mbm), and no pair is a certificate. Each pair's failure is a separate congruence fact, so the shortest 'proof of failure' is the full list; no covering by fewer moduli is possible.
not_done: No comparison across the 9 failures; no check of whether failure proofs share a shape.
next: Compare the failure trial sets of the 9 known (★)-failures.

summary: Among the 105 hard primes (R/M_BM<0.25, p≤10^6) the residue distribution mod 840 is strongly non-uniform (chi^2=660 on 96 df). Class 409 (mod 840) holds 13 hard primes (expected 1.1); at R/M<0.5 it holds 71 (expected 11.6). By Legendre cells (3/p),(5/p),(7/p): all-QR cell (+,+,+) holds 50 of 105 hard primes against a 12.4% base rate; hard primes are never in (−,−,−),(−,−,+),(−,+,−),(−,+,+) cells except 4 in (−,−,+). The signal is a residual dependence on quadratic characters mod 105 that M_BM does not absorb (interpretation, not checked against M_gen).
not_done: Not tested against M_gen or higher-modulus classes (mod 2520); quartic-symbol part (Z1803) confounded with this.
next: Recompute residual vs M_gen and mod 2520 classes; check class 409 at p>10^6.

summary: Quartic symbols (2/p)_4,(3/p)_4,(5/p)_4,(7/p)_4 among p≡1 (mod 8): on the hard set (n≈105) the distribution of (5/p)_4 and (7/p)_4 differs from controls (e.g. (7/p)_4 ∈ {±i} 28% vs 50%), but the hard set is concentrated in the quadratic cell and class 409 (Z1802), so the quartic effect is not separated from the quadratic-cell effect. Result: no independent quartic invariant established.
not_done: No separation of quartic from quadratic-cell effects (would need controls matched on (3,5,7)-cells).
next: Match controls on the (3/p),(5/p),(7/p) cell before reading quartic symbols.

summary: The question (|T(p)| ≤ (1-δ)M0(p) asymptotically) is answered in BM_CORRECTED_COUNT.md §2 (Thm 2.2 proof, line ~133): T(p) = o(L^2) hence M_BM(p) = M0(p)(1+o(1)), proved via the hyperbola decomposition and Dirichlet-series bounds. Data check: sup over p≡1 (mod 4) of T/M0 is 0.528 (p=73), 0.443 (10^3–10^4), 0.387 (10^4–10^5), 0.349 (10^5–10^6): decreasing, consistent with T=o(M0).
not_done: Explicit δ(p) not extracted; the bound is asymptotic.

summary: Analytic: sum_{u,B} chi(u)chi(B)/phi(4uB) is a hyperbola-truncated sum (uB ≤ p/4), not an Euler product, so identification with L(1,chi)^2 holds only up to a truncation error that is not controlled here; no Mellin inversion carried out.
not_done: No numerical test of T(p) against L(1,chi_p)^2.

summary: The pairing d↔e is the swap (u,B)→(B,u): d=(p+u)/B maps to e=(p+B)/u (identity asserted in scripts/z52d_p2_TO5_certs.c). It is fixed-point-free on P(p) because u=B forces u=B=1, excluded by u+B odd; hence R(p) is even. Checked: all 39175 primes p≡1 (mod 4), p≤10^6 have even R. Exact hyperbola error tracking was not done.

Solutions of 4/(kp)=1/x+1/y+1/z (unordered) for p∈{13,17,29,37,53,409} and k up to 12–20: the descent solutions (k dividing all three denominators, i.e. the 4/p solutions scaled) number 4, 4, 7, 9, 13, 15 respectively and are a vanishing fraction: p=13, k=12 has 378 solutions of which 4 descend. Transports from kp to p are therefore not tautological in the typical case, and the descent reading does not reduce the problem.
next: Test whether non-descending solutions can be lifted by a gcd condition.

summary: Same enumeration as Z1812: the non-descending solutions are those where k does not divide all three denominators (e.g. p=13, k=2: 16 of 20 solutions; p=409, k=2: 63 of 78). The partial-gcd subclass (k divides exactly two) was not separated.
next: Count denominators divisible by k in each solution.

summary: Analytic: the forbidden-class density sum_{4uC-1 ≤ B} 1/(4uC-1) grows like log^2 B, far above 1, so a lower-bound avoidance sieve at level B is outside the regime where Rosser–Iwaniec-type minorants are positive; B1 already yields evaders, so no unconditional lower bound follows from this route (Assessment).

Analytic: 4Cp+1 with C fixed is a linear form in p; a Maynard–Tao argument could make several of them prime simultaneously, and prime 4Cp+1 kills slice C (verified: 25682 prime-N slices, 0 successes). This gives a menu-evasion family but no new certificate statement.

Premise verified: for prime N=4Cp+1 the C-slice never succeeds (25682 slices, C≤40, p≡1 (mod 4), p≤10^5: 0 successes). Semiprime and higher slices succeed with rates Ω=2: 0.044, Ω=3: 0.112, Ω=4: 0.19, Ω=5: 0.28, Ω=6: 0.35, Ω=7: 0.41 (scripts/z52d_p2_TO5_slices.py).
not_done: No closed formula for the success rate by factorisation type.
next: Use the Ω-table as the calibration for slice-success models.

summary: Prime-modulus slices: a certificate with d=(p+u)/B prime exists iff some prime ℓ | 4Cp+1 with 4C | ℓ+1 and p ≡ -(4C)^{-1} mod ℓ. Over p≡1 (mod 4): P(exists such ℓ ≤ L) = 0.50 (L=3), 0.83 (L=31), 0.90 (L=101), 0.97 (L=1001), 0.990 (L=10^4). The uncovered fraction decays as L^{-0.50} (log-log slope -0.50 on [10^3,10^5], -0.52 on [10^5,10^6]). The premise 'sum tau((ℓ+1)/4)/ℓ matches log^2' is false: the sum over ℓ≤L, ℓ≡3 (4) is 2.58, 3.89, 5.24 at L=10^3,10^4,10^5, i.e. ≈ ½ log L, which explains the L^{-1/2} decay. Prime-d certificates are 47% of all certificates for p<10^3 but 25% for p∈[10^5,10^6].
not_done: No rigorous covering theorem; the L^{-1/2} law is empirical up to 10^6 and the heuristic is Π(1-τ/ℓ) under CRT independence.
next: Test the L^{-1/2} law for p up to 10^7 and check whether the uncovered set is the (★)-failure-like set.

summary: Same data as Z1821: the union over primes ℓ of the classes -(4C)^{-1} mod ℓ (C | (ℓ+1)/4) covers all but ≈ L^{-1/2} of the primes up to L. Since the total class density Σ τ/ℓ diverges (≈½ log L), density arguments do not exclude a covering of all primes, but CRT evaders (B1) exist; no new statement.

Route test: -1 ∈ ⟨classes of prime factors of 4Cp+1⟩ mod 4C holds for 25% of hard-prime slices (C≤30) but -1 is a subproduct (divisor residue) in only 2.9%: the subgroup/Artin gate overcounts ≈9× and is not the operative condition. For the 9 (★)-failures the subgroup test still holds in 18.5% of slices (50/270), while the subproduct test never does.
next: Use the subproduct gate, not the subgroup gate, in any Artin-type model.

summary: corr(R/M_BM, log tau(p+1)) = +0.53 and corr(R/M_BM, log tau_3(p+1)) = +0.533 over 4783 primes p≡1 (mod 4), p≤10^5. The association is mechanical: the B=1 slice counts divisors of p+1 that are ≡3 (mod 4); tau_3 adds nothing beyond tau.
not_done: No τ_3 comparison with R beyond the B=1 slice.
next: Remove the B=1 slice and re-test.

summary: Analytic: the Dirichlet series D(s)=sum R(n) n^{-s} has no visible product formula; the triple-pole heuristic is consistent with the log^2 mean but was not verified.

Calibration of the random subset-product model: for squarefree semiprimes N=4Cm+1 the success rate (q≡-1 mod 4C for a factor q) is below the naive 1/phi(4C) for φ(4C)≥8 (ratio success·φ ≈ 0.3–0.6), but for balanced semiprimes (both factors > N^{1/3}) the ratio returns to ≈0.8–1.2 (C=6: 0.12 vs 0.125; C=13: 0.035 vs 0.042; C=21: 0.049 vs 0.042; C=24: 0.030 vs 0.031). The deficit comes from small factors (q < N^{1/3}) that cannot be ≡-1 mod 4C in range. Same behaviour for N from primes p and from all odd m, so it is not a prime-p effect.
not_done: Only semiprimes; no full subset-product distribution for k≥3 factors.

summary: Analytic: ES is not a system of linear divisibilities with fixed unknowns (the C-variable enters multiplicatively with u), so a local-global theorem for linear divisibility does not apply directly.

Lemma (proof attempt, checked on the definition): D(N,m) := ∃ d | N with d ≡ −1 (mod m) has an NP witness (the divisor d). For the complement, a witness is a factorisation N = ∏ q_i^{e_i} with each q_i prime certified by a Pratt certificate; this has size poly(log N) and the divisor set is then enumerated in time d(N)·poly(log N) = N^{o(1)}. Hence D(N,m) ∈ NP ∩ coNP, so the ES slice predicate has no complexity barrier beyond the availability of factorisations. Nothing computed; the statement is a lemma with the argument above.
not_done: No computation; the NP∩coNP claim uses the standard Pratt-certificate fact (not re-proved here).

summary: Criterion check: the B=1 slice succeeds iff (p+1)/2 has a prime factor ≡3 (mod 4). Verified for all 39175 primes p≡1 (mod 4), p≤10^6 (100% agreement). Failure fractions 0.100 on [5,10^3), 0.146 on [10^3,10^4), 0.140 on [10^4,10^5), 0.126 on [10^5,10^6), and c/√log p fits with c≈0.45 on [10^3,10^6]: the Landau–Ramanujan shape. Iterated Landau–Ramanujan for consecutive shifts: over p≡1 (mod 4), p≤10^6, the probability that all of the slices B=1..6 fail is 0.00605, versus 0.00164 for the product of marginal failure rates: a factor 3.7. Failures of the shift slices are strongly positively correlated, so the independence heuristic (product of (log p)^{-δ_B}) underestimates joint failure by about 4× here. Exact for B=1,2; approximate for B≥3 (no gcd filter).
